Hi Sarah / MediBridge team —

Thanks again for the demo earlier today. Quick recap from our side and the items we promised to follow up on related to HIPAA/PHI handling and BAA availability: 

Summary of capabilities (high-level)
- BAA: Redwood can execute a BAA for customers that choose Dedicated (reserved capacity) or Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments.
- PHI handling: Full PHI processing is supported on Private (customer-managed network/on-prem) and Dedicated with VPC peering and optional customer KMS/HSM key control. Hosted (public API) is not recommended for PHI unless you adopt strict anonymization/tokenization upstream — we cannot sign BAA for hosted endpoints.
- SOC 2: We are SOC 2 Type II in production; see attached SOC2 summary for the current reporting period.
- Data residency: We can pin deployments to specific US regions (us-east-1, us-west-2) for Dedicated/Private.

Action items we suggested / next asks from you
1) Confirm that MediBridge requires a signed BAA to proceed with PHI (you indicated yes on the call).
2) Confirm desired deployment model (Private VPC, Dedicated with VPC peering, or non-PHI on Hosted).
3) Provide any procurement or legal contact for DocuSign routing so we can circulate our BAA template.
4) Security evidence: we will provide SOC2 summary + dataflow diagram. Please confirm if a full SOC2 report is required vs. summary + auditor contact.

Attachments: Redwood_BAA_Options.pdf (BAA paths/requirements), Redwood_SOC2-Summary.pdf (summary).

Proposed next steps
- If you confirm BAA + Dedicated/Private, we aim to: deliver SOC2 evidence and a dataflow diagram within 3 business days, circulate the BAA for signature within 1 week.
- If procurement wants to accelerate, loop in procurement@medibridge.com and we’ll prioritize a DocuSign flow.

If helpful I can schedule a short follow-up with our security lead to walk through the dataflow and keys.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — looping in a few specifics from our legal and ops side so your procurement/security team has concrete answers: 

Eligible deployment modes for PHI (Redwood)
- Private (VPC / on-prem): Full PHI allowed; customer controls networking and can use on-prem KMS/HSM. This is the only model where on-prem deployments are possible.
- Dedicated (reserved GPU pools): Full PHI allowed with VPC peering and optional customer-managed keys (KMS integration). Data can be pinned to US regions (we support us-east-1 and us-west-2).
- Hosted API (public): Not supported for PHI when a BAA is required. Hosted is acceptable for de-identified or tokenized data only; we cannot sign a BAA for hosted endpoints.

Key management options
- Customer-managed KMS (recommended for PHI): supported in Dedicated and Private.
- HSM-backed key options are available for Private deployments; our team can provide a short tech note on HSM integration.

Required evidence we can provide quickly
- SOC 2 Type II summary (attached) + auditor contact.
- Sample dataflow diagram for Dedicated/Private (attached: deployment-dataflow.png).

Procurement ask / timeline
- Please confirm procurement@medibridge.com as the DocuSign target; we will send our standard BAA template.
- If you need full SOC2 report, indicate that in reply and we will request a redacted copy from our auditors (may take 2–3 business days).

I’ll start the BAA routing once procurement confirms the DocuSign address. Happy to set up a 30-min security deep-dive with our security engineer next week.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Head of Legal Ops | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai
